notes: WHICH COLUMNS THESE INDEXES REFER TO. Not the client's own sjabloon: `HRM 5_Grondslag Vakantietoeslag.xlsx` holds only three columns (Medewerker, Bedrag, Grondslag), and four of the eight AFAS fields below cannot be filled from it. The indexes above follow the **enriched** seven-column dataset Taroen's conversion script produces (`SetHeaders`, in this exact order): 0 Medewerker, 1 Werkgever, 2 Periodetabel, 3 Datum, 4 Boekjaar, 5 Periode, 6 Waarde. `file`/`sheet` are therefore left empty, the same as erp-projecten.json and hrm-medewerkers.json, because this mapping was not made by dropping a workbook on the page. If the enriched dataset is ever saved as a real sheet, drop it on /afas/updateconnectors and every field re-points itself by header name (`remapToSheet`).

WHERE THE SEVEN COLUMNS COME FROM, which is the thing to understand before trusting this mapping — and it is the first mapping where all three of the tool's eventual sources appear at once (see docs/afas-integration.md#where-a-value-comes-from):  (1) THE CLIENT'S SHEET — **Medewerker** and **Grondslag** (which becomes **Waarde**), the only two columns the client actually fills.  (2) CONFIGURATION on the project or the dossieritem — the **Periodetabel** behind `PtId`, and the **livegangdatum** (01-01-2026 in the script, hard-coded there) that the date calculation floors against. Neither belongs in a client sheet: they are settings of the conversion, the same for every row.  (3) A GET CONNECTOR against the customer's AFAS — the medewerker's **datum in dienst**, read per employee, plus **Werkgever**, which is employee data rather than something a client should retype.  And on top of those three, DERIVED values: Datum = max(datum in dienst, livegangdatum), Boekjaar = that date's year, Periode = that date's month. So five of the seven columns are not sheet data at all. Until the tool can read configuration and call GET connectors itself, Taroen's script stands in for all of it and this mapping describes the shape its output has — which is why the column list above is authoritative and the sjabloon is not.
Looncomponent (`Sc02`) is a FIXED 601 — 'Looncomponent is always 601' per Taroen. `Sc02` is an int (len 4) and AFAS reports no allowed-value list for it, so 601 is written as a number, not a string.

`Id` (Regelnummer) is left unmapped on purpose and is NOT a blocker. AFAS's metainfo marks it mandatory, but that applies to an **update**: this conversion only ever **creates** loonmutaties (POST), and on a create AFAS assigns the regelnummer itself. Worth knowing generally, because metainfo does not distinguish the two: a field flagged mandatory that is a system-assigned key or line number is likely required only when updating, so the flag alone is not evidence that a conversion has a gap. The two mappings that leaned on the older reading have since been re-read in this light and confirmed live (08-09-2026): `FiEntries#EnNo` (erp-openstaandposten) POSTs 201 with the field omitted and AFAS returns the number it assigned, incrementing across two identical calls, and `HrEmployeeMobility#SeNo` (hrm-wagenpark) behaves the same — so the rule holds for all three and neither module is blocked by its volgnummer. See docs/todo.md under Done.

The sjabloon's `Bedrag` column is deliberately NOT converted — it is there for the user's own convenience (a readable 'bedrag nog uit te betalen vakantietoeslag' beside the grondslag), not as input for AFAS. Only `Grondslag` becomes a value, on looncomponent 601. So `VaD2`/`VaD3` stay empty and there is no second looncomponent and no second record per medewerker. Recorded explicitly because an unmapped numeric column in a three-column sheet otherwise reads as an oversight.

SYSTEMIC — the date format is wrong for AFAS, and not only here. `DaTi` receives the script's `Datum` as `01-01-2026` (DD-MM-YYYY, which is also what every rule set validates: 'DD-MM-YYYY | DD/MM/YYYY'), but every date in every payload example in docs/AFAS-Profit-API-Referentie.md is **ISO** — `2023-01-01` or `2024-07-11T08:00:00` — and the doc contains no DD-MM-YYYY at all. `afasValue()` converts only int/decimal/boolean and passes a date column through as the text it was, so today a mapped date column sends the Dutch notation straight to AFAS. Note the asymmetry that proves it is an oversight rather than a decision: a **fixed** date is converted properly (`parseFixedValue()` appends `T00:00:00` to an ISO input), so fixed dates are right and column dates are not. This affects all 27 date columns across all 14 modules, not just this field; recorded in docs/todo.md under *Row-level transforms*.

Left unmapped, none of them required: `Ds` (Omschrijving — a free text on the mutation, e.g. 'Conversie vakantietoeslag', a good candidate for a fixed value if the business wants the rows recognisable in AFAS), `EmDp`/`CrId`/`CcId` (organisatorische eenheid, kostenplaats, kostendrager — all derivable from the medewerker in AFAS rather than from this sheet), `EnSe` (Dienstverband — the same which-employment ambiguity already flagged on hrm-verlofsaldo, hrm-salarisparameters and hrm-uitzendkrachten, and it matters here for a medewerker with more than one dienstverband), `FuId`, `Rem`, `VaD2`/`VaD3` (see the Bedrag question above), `ViTr`/`ViTv` (WPM-rapportage vervoermiddel and type reis — irrelevant to vakantietoeslag) and the four custom fields (`Voorcalculatie`, `Abonnement`, `Voorcalculatieregel GUID`, `Werkbonnummer`).

Not grouped: one medewerker is one loonmutatie, so the ordinary one-row-one-record path applies. HrCompMut has no nested object at all (24 fields, zero objects), so there is nothing a group key could repeat even if the data called for it.
`hrm-vakantietoeslag` has no deeltaakcode in AFAS, so this module can never appear for a project today (see docs/todo.md). This mapping is groundwork; nothing converts through it until that changes.
